Earlier, in **Basel**, the **Deep Heat Mining** project had been stopped after noticeable earthquakes in 2006. St Gallen had therefore deliberately chosen a different method.

gewusst: The temperature at depth was exactly right; the only problem was that the amount of water was too small.
Other geothermal projects in Switzerland now learn from the experience of Basel and St Gallen.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is about 41,300 square kilometres in size. That is small compared with many countries in Europe, yet on this area there are mountains, lakes, forests, fields and cities.
wichtigste: Switzerland is about 41,300 km² in size.
From west to east it measures about 350 km, from north to south about 220 km.
The Alps take up about 60 per cent of the area.
About a quarter of the area is unproductive, such as rock, glaciers and waters.
A good third is used for farming, alpine pastures included.
Settlements make up about 8 per cent of the area.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland measures about **41,300 km²**. From **Chancy** in the west to the **Val Müstair** in the east it is about **350 km** as the crow flies. From **Bargen** in the north to **Chiasso** in the south it is about **220 km**. By train you can cross the country in a day.

Germany is about **357,000 km²** in size. If you divide this number by the area of Switzerland, you get about 8.6. So Switzerland fits about **9 times** into Germany. Even so, Switzerland is bigger than Belgium, for example.

Switzerland consists of three **major landscapes**. The **Alps** cover about 60 per cent of the area, the **Central Plateau** about 30 per cent and the **Jura** about 10 per cent. Most people, however, live on the Central Plateau, because the land is flatter there.

The **Federal Statistical Office** measures with the **land use statistics** how the ground is used. According to the survey of 2018, about **a quarter** is unproductive: rock, scree, glaciers and waters. About **36 per cent** is **agricultural land**, alpine pastures included. Just under a third is **forest**. The **settlement area** with houses, roads and railway lines makes up just under **8 per cent** and grows mainly on the Central Plateau.

gewusst: If you pressed the mountains of Switzerland flat, their area would be much bigger than 41,300 km².
Forest covers almost as much of the area of Switzerland as agriculture does.

teile.einleitung: On 28 May 2025, the Birch Glacier broke off above the village of Blatten in the Lötschental. Ice and rock buried almost the whole village, which had been evacuated in time.
wichtigste: On 28 May 2025 the Birch Glacier broke off above Blatten.
Beforehand, rock from the Kleines Nesthorn had been falling onto the glacier for days.
Millions of tonnes of rock debris overloaded the glacier until it collapsed.
On 19 May 2025 the authorities ordered the evacuation.
Around 90 per cent of the village was buried.
The Lonza was dammed into a lake.

abschnitte.text: From mid-May 2025 the rock face of the **Kleines Nesthorn** became unstable. In several rockfalls, rock fell onto the **Birch Glacier** below. By the end of May, about 9 million tonnes of rock lay on the ice. Even in the years before, the glacier's snout had unusually **advanced**, because more and more debris weighed on it.

The Birch Glacier had been observed since an **ice collapse in December 1993**. That is why experts recognised the danger early. On **19 May 2025** the authorities ordered the **evacuation** of Blatten. Around 300 people had to leave their homes within a short time. The early evacuation prevented a large number of casualties.

On **28 May 2025** the overloaded glacier collapsed almost completely. Ice, rock and debris plunged into the valley. The **Swiss Seismological Service** recorded a signal of **magnitude 3.1**. Around **90 per cent** of the village of Blatten was buried, including about 130 houses and the church.

abschnitte.titel: A new lake and the consequences
abschnitte.text: The masses of debris blocked the river **Lonza** and dammed it into a **lake**. This flooded parts of the village that had not been buried. The **Swiss Insurance Association** estimated the insured damage at around **320 million francs**. Forest, farmland and a nature reserve were also lost.

gewusst: The debris cone above Blatten is in places up to 100 metres thick.
Before the collapse, the ice was moving at about 10 metres a day.

teile.einleitung: The Gotthard Road Tunnel carries cars and lorries under the Gotthard Pass. It links German-speaking Switzerland with Ticino and is one of the most important roads across the Alps.
wichtigste: The tunnel runs between Göschenen in Uri and Airolo in Ticino.
The A2 motorway runs through it.
At around 17 km it is the longest road tunnel in the Alps.
On 24 October 2001 a serious fire broke out after a lorry accident.
In 2016 the people voted in favour of building a second tube.
The second tube is due to open around 2030.

abschnitte.text: The **Gotthard Road Tunnel** runs between **Göschenen** in the canton of Uri and **Airolo** in Ticino. It is around **17 km** long and opened in **1980**. The **A2** motorway runs through it. It is the **longest road tunnel in the Alps**.

Today there is only **one tube**. In it, cars drive in **two-way traffic**, that is, in both directions side by side. This is demanding and requires great care. Lorries may only drive with a gap between them. In the holidays, long **traffic jams** often form in front of the tunnel.

On **24 October 2001**, two lorries collided in the tunnel. A **serious fire** broke out, in which eleven people lost their lives. Safety was improved afterwards. Since then, for example, stricter rules apply to lorries, and there are more refuges.

The tunnel is old and has to be **renovated**. So that it is not closed for long while this happens, a **second tube** is being built. The people voted for this in **2016**. The new tube is due to open around **2030**. After that the old tube will be renewed. Later, only one lane per direction is to be used in each tube.

gewusst: A safety tunnel runs parallel to the road tunnel, and people can escape through it in an emergency.
Above the tunnel, the pass road over the Gotthard is still open in summer.

teile.einleitung: The **Energy Strategy 2050** is the Confederation’s plan for Switzerland’s energy supply. It relies on using less energy, more renewable energy and a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy. The voters accepted important parts of it at the ballot box.
wichtigste: The strategy is based on efficiency, renewable energy and a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy.
The trigger was the reactor disaster at Fukushima in March 2011.
On 21 May 2017 the people accepted the new Energy Act with 58.2 per cent.
Since then no general licences may be granted for new nuclear power plants.
On 9 June 2024 the Electricity Act was accepted with 68.7 per cent.
The Mühleberg nuclear power plant was switched off in December 2019.

abschnitte.text: The Energy Strategy 2050 has three pillars. First, less energy is to be used, which is called **efficiency**. Second, **renewable energy** is to be expanded, for example water, sun and wind. Third, Switzerland is leaving **nuclear energy** step by step. Existing nuclear power plants may keep running as long as they are safe.

In **March 2011** a serious reactor disaster occurred at the Japanese nuclear power plant **Fukushima Daiichi**. After that the **Federal Council** and **Parliament** decided on a step-by-step exit from nuclear energy. On **20 December 2019** the energy company BKW took the **Mühleberg** nuclear power plant off the grid for economic reasons. It was the first Swiss commercial nuclear power plant to be shut down for good, and it has been dismantled ever since.

A **referendum** was called against the new **Energy Act**. On **21 May 2017**, **58.2 per cent** voted in favour. So the first package of measures came into force in **2018**. Since then no **general licences** may be granted for new nuclear power plants any more. The **grid surcharge** on every kilowatt hour used rose from 1.5 to at most **2.3 centimes**. It finances support payments for renewable energy and the restoration of waters.

On **9 June 2024** the voters accepted the **Electricity Act**, also called the **“Mantelerlass”**, with **68.7 per cent**. It makes it easier to build large hydro, wind and solar plants. By **2035** at least **35 terawatt hours** of electricity a year are to be produced from renewable energy without hydropower, for example from sun, wind and biomass. That is many times today’s production from these sources.

By 2050 Switzerland is pursuing the goal of **net zero**. This means that no more greenhouse gases are emitted than natural and technical stores can absorb. For this, fossil energy must be largely replaced by electricity from renewable sources. Part of the **CO2 levy** on heating oil and natural gas flows into the **Buildings Programme** of the Confederation and the cantons. It supports heat insulation and renewable heating systems.

gewusst: On the Energy Act and the Electricity Act the people had the last word at the ballot box.
In 2019 Mühleberg in the canton of Bern was the first Swiss nuclear power plant to be switched off for ever.

teile.einleitung: The Great Aletsch Glacier in the Valais is the largest glacier in the Alps. It is around 20 kilometres long and belongs to the Jungfrau-Aletsch UNESCO World Heritage Site. Because of climate change it is melting fast.
wichtigste: The Great Aletsch Glacier is the largest glacier in the Alps.
At the Konkordiaplatz the ice is over 900 metres thick.
The area has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2001.
In 2017 it covered around 78 square kilometres, compared with around 105 in 1850.
The river Massa is formed from its meltwater.
Dark stripes on the ice are called medial moraines.

abschnitte.text: A **glacier** is a huge mass of ice that moves slowly down a valley. The Great Aletsch Glacier is formed from several firn streams. The longest tributary is the **Great Aletsch Firn** at around 9 kilometres. Then there are the **Jungfraufirn** and the **Grüneggfirn**. They flow together at the **Konkordiaplatz**. There the ice is more than **900 metres** thick.

Glacier ice moves slowly. Near the Konkordiaplatz the Aletsch Glacier flows at up to about **180 metres a year**. When two arms of a glacier flow together, their edges of rubble join to form a **medial moraine**. On the Aletsch Glacier these can be seen as long, dark stripes. The meltwater flows south as the **Massa** and joins the Rhône above Naters.

Above the glacier's snout lies the **Aletsch Forest**. It grows on an old lateral moraine near the **Riederfurka**. There stand many old **Swiss stone pines** and larches. The forest is protected. From the **Eggishorn** above Fiesch there is a famous view of the glacier, and also from the Riederalp and the Bettmeralp.

In December **2001** the Jungfrau-Aletsch area was added to the **UNESCO World Heritage** list. It was the first natural heritage site in the Alps. Later the area was enlarged. Today it is called **Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch**. World Heritage means that a place is especially valuable to the whole of humanity.

Since about 1850 the Aletsch Glacier has shrunk greatly. At that time it covered around **105 square kilometres**, and in **2017** only around **78**. The main cause is the **warming of the climate**. In the past the glacier dammed the **Märjelensee**. When this lake burst out suddenly, there were serious floods on the Massa in the 19th century.

gewusst: At the Konkordiaplatz you could stack several tall towers one on top of another under the thick ice.
The glacier's snout has retreated by several kilometres since 1850.

teile.einleitung: The **Eiger** is one of the best-known mountains in Switzerland. It stands in the Bernese Oberland above Grindelwald. Its steep **north face** is world-famous and was long regarded as one of the most dangerous walls in the Alps.
wichtigste: The Eiger is about 3,967 metres high and stands in the canton of Bern.
Below the Eiger lies the village of Grindelwald.
The Eiger north face is about 1,650 metres high.
In 1858 Charles Barrington of Ireland was the first to stand on the summit.
In 1938 Heckmair, Vörg, Harrer and Kasparek climbed the north face.
The Jungfrau Railway runs through the Eiger in a tunnel.

abschnitte.titel: A mountain in the Bernese Oberland
abschnitte.text: The **Eiger** is about **3,967 metres** high. It stands in the **canton of Bern**, in the Bernese Oberland. Together with the **Mönch** and the **Jungfrau** it forms a famous trio. Directly below its north face lies the village of **Grindelwald**. From there you can see the dark wall rising steeply.

In **1858** a person reached the summit for the first time. It was the Irishman **Charles Barrington**. On 11 August 1858 he climbed up with the Grindelwald mountain guides **Christian Almer** and **Peter Bohren**. They did not choose the north face but an easier route.

The **Eiger north face** is about **1,650 metres** high. It is among the best-known and most difficult rock walls in the Alps. Falling stones and sudden changes in the weather made it feared. From **21 to 24 July 1938** the first climb was achieved. Anderl **Heckmair**, Ludwig **Vörg**, Heinrich **Harrer** and Fritz **Kasparek** managed it together.

The **Jungfrau Railway** runs in a long tunnel through the Eiger and the Mönch up to the **Jungfraujoch**. In the middle of the mountain it stops at the **Eismeer station**. There travellers look through large windows at glaciers. The earlier Eigerwand station has no longer been served since 2016. Since **December 2020** the **Eiger Express** cable car has brought visitors quickly from Grindelwald to the **Eigergletscher** station.

gewusst: The Jungfrau Railway stops in the middle of the Eiger so that you can look at the ice through windows.
The first climb of the north face in 1938 took four days.

teile.einleitung: The **Engadine** is a long high valley in the canton of Graubünden. Through the valley flows the Inn, called “En” in Romansh, from which the Engadine takes its name. It is known for lakes, mountains, old customs and St Moritz.
wichtigste: The Engadine lies in the canton of Graubünden in the east of Switzerland.
The Inn is called “En” in Romansh and gives the valley its name.
Many people there speak Romansh.
St Moritz hosted the Winter Olympics in 1928 and 1948.
On 1 March the children celebrate Chalandamarz.
The water of the Inn flows via the Danube into the Black Sea.

abschnitte.text: The Engadine is a long **high valley** in the canton of **Graubünden**. It begins at the Maloja Pass and stretches north-east as far as the border with Austria. People distinguish the **Upper Engadine** with its lakes and the **Lower Engadine**. Through the valley flows the **Inn**. In Romansh it is called **“En”**, and that is where the name Engadine comes from.

In the Engadine many people speak **Romansh** as well as German, one of the four national languages of Switzerland. An old custom is **Chalandamarz** on 1 March. Then the children go through the village with **bells** and drive away the winter. The children’s book **“Schellen-Ursli”** (“Ursli and the Cowbell”) tells of it too. At the festival Ursli wants to carry the biggest bell, and the story is set in **Guarda**.

abschnitte.titel: St Moritz and the ski marathon
abschnitte.text: The well-known holiday resort of **St Moritz** lies in the Upper Engadine. The Winter Olympics took place there in **1928** and **1948**. Every year the **Engadin Ski Marathon** takes place. Thousands of people run on cross-country skis from **Maloja** to **S-chanf**. At **Pontresina** the car-free **Val Roseg** branches off. Many guests go there by horse-drawn carriage to the Roseg Glacier.

A well-known speciality is the **Engadine nut tart**. It is filled with **walnuts** and **caramel**. The Inn flows from the Engadine to **Austria** and enters the **Danube** at **Passau**. The Danube flows all the way to the **Black Sea**. In this way water from the Engadine travels very far to the east.

gewusst: The Engadine is named after its river: the Inn is called “En” in Romansh.
Water from the Engadine flows via the Inn and the Danube as far as the Black Sea.

teile.einleitung: The glaciers in Switzerland are getting smaller because it keeps getting warmer. This decline is called glacier retreat. It is greatly changing the landscape of the Alps.
wichtigste: There are around 1,400 glaciers in Switzerland.
The main cause of glacier retreat is global warming.
The Alpine glaciers last reached a great peak around 1850.
In 2022 the Swiss glaciers lost about 6 per cent of their ice.
In 2019 the Pizol Glacier was bid farewell with a funeral ceremony.
Where a glacier melts, stones and often a new lake are left behind.

abschnitte.text: A glacier is a large mass of ice that forms from snow. If more ice melts in summer than snow is added in winter, it shrinks. The main cause is **global warming**: temperatures are rising. There are around **1,400 glaciers** in Switzerland, and almost all of them are getting smaller.

Around **1850** the Alpine glaciers reached their last great **peak**. Since then they have been retreating, and in recent decades ever faster. In **2022** the Swiss glaciers lost about **6 per cent** of their ice, more than ever measured. At the **Morteratsch Glacier**, **signs with dates** along the path show where the ice used to be.

The **Pizol Glacier** in the St Gallen Alps has shrunk so much that it is hardly considered a glacier any more. In **2019**, people bid it farewell with a **funeral ceremony**. They wanted to show how serious glacier retreat is. At the **Rhône Glacier**, part of the ice is covered with **white sheets** in summer so that it melts more slowly.

abschnitte.titel: What remains and what is missing
abschnitte.text: Where a glacier disappears, **stones**, debris and sometimes a **new lake** are often left behind. In summer the **meltwater** is important for the **rivers**, for hydropower plants and for farming. If the glaciers get smaller, this water will one day be missing in hot summers.

gewusst: The white sheets on the Rhône Glacier reflect sunlight back and so slow down the melting.
Some glaciers in Switzerland could disappear completely by the end of this century.

teile.einleitung: The **Ceneri Base Tunnel** is a railway tunnel in the canton of Ticino. It runs under the Monte Ceneri and is the last big building block of the new flat railway through the Alps. Since it opened, Lugano and Locarno have moved much closer together.
wichtigste: The Ceneri Base Tunnel passes under the Monte Ceneri between Bellinzona and Lugano.
It is part of the NEAT, together with the Gotthard Base Tunnel.
The tunnel consists of two single-track tubes with cross passages.
The rock was mostly blasted, not bored.
The main breakthrough took place in January 2016.
The journey time from Locarno to Lugano was halved to around 30 minutes.

abschnitte.text: The **Monte Ceneri Pass** lies at about 554 metres above sea level. It separates the area around Bellinzona from the area around Lugano. The pass is not high, but for heavy **freight trains** the gradient was nevertheless an obstacle. The **north portal** of the tunnel lies at Vigana in the municipality of Camorino, the **south portal** at **Vezia** near Lugano. The tunnel is around 15 kilometres long.

abschnitte.titel: The flat railway through the Alps
abschnitte.text: The Ceneri Base Tunnel belongs to the **NEAT**, the New Rail Link through the Alps. Together with the Gotthard Base Tunnel it forms a **flat railway**. That means trains can travel through the Alps almost without any gradient. Without the Ceneri, heavy freight trains would have had to climb a gradient once more before Lugano. Only with it is the route flat all the way.

At the Gotthard, huge **tunnel boring machines** did most of the work. At the Ceneri, by contrast, the rock was mostly excavated by **drill and blast**. In this method holes are drilled into the rock, filled with explosive, and then the rock is cleared away. In **January 2016** the **main breakthrough** took place. After that tracks, railway technology and safety systems were installed.

As at the Gotthard, the trains run in **two separate single-track tubes**. In each tube the trains go in only one direction. **Cross passages** join the two tubes. In an emergency, passengers can in this way escape into the other, safe tube.

Since it opened in 2020, especially people in Ticino have benefited. The journey time between **Locarno** and **Lugano** has been halved to around **30 minutes**. Bellinzona and Lugano are also linked faster. In this way Ticino has grown together into one connected **suburban railway area**.

gewusst: Thanks to the tunnel, the journey from Locarno to Lugano takes only about half as long as before.
Only with the Ceneri Base Tunnel is the Gotthard axis flat all the way to Lugano.

teile.einleitung: During the ice ages a large part of Switzerland was covered by thick glaciers. The ice planed out valleys, created lakes and left marks in the rock. The landscape of Switzerland is still strongly shaped by these times today.
wichtigste: The last great cold period in the Alps is traditionally called the Würm glaciation.
About 24,000 years ago the glaciers were at their greatest extent.
At that time the Rhône Glacier reached from the Valais as far as the area of Solothurn.
About 11,700 years ago the last ice age came to an end.
Many lakes on the Central Plateau lie in basins that glaciers scooped out.
The Little Ice Age lasted from about 1300 to 1850.

abschnitte.text: The last great cold period in the Alps is traditionally called the **Würm glaciation**. In Switzerland people also speak of the **Birrfeld glaciation**. About **24,000 years ago** the glaciers were at their greatest extent. At that time ice covered large parts of the **Central Plateau**. About **11,700 years ago** the ice age came to an end. Since then we have been living in a warm period, the **Holocene**.

The glaciers flowed out of the Alps far into the lowlands. The ice-age **Rhône Glacier** flowed from the Valais across the area of Lake Geneva into the Central Plateau. It reached as far as the area of **Solothurn** and **Wangen an der Aare**. Other glaciers too, for example from the Reuss Valley or the Linth area, pushed far to the north.

Many large lakes on the Central Plateau owe their origin to the glaciers, for example **Lake Zurich**. The ice deepened valleys and **scooped out basins**. When the glaciers melted, these basins filled with water. Often the lake was also dammed by **moraines**. Moraines are ridges of stones and debris that a glacier leaves behind.

Glaciers leave typical marks. Stones on the underside of the ice grind the rock smooth and scratch grooves into it. In this way a **glacial polish** arises. The scratches show in which direction the ice flowed. Under the glacier **meltwater** also swirled in circles carrying stones. These stones ground round, deep holes into the rock, the **potholes**, called **Gletschertöpfe** in German.

Even after the last ice age the climate fluctuated. Roughly between **1300 and 1850** there was a cooler period that is called the **Little Ice Age**. The summers were cooler, and the Alpine glaciers advanced several times. Some villages in the Alps were threatened at that time by growing glaciers. Since the end of that period the glaciers have been melting back again.

gewusst: Lake Zurich lies in a basin that an ice-age glacier scooped out.
At the Glacier Garden in Lucerne you can see potholes from the Ice Age.

teile.einleitung: Cross-border commuters live abroad and work in Switzerland. Every day or every week they cross the border. There are especially many in Geneva, Basel and Ticino.
wichtigste: In the second quarter of 2026, according to the FSO, around 414,000 foreign cross-border commuters worked in Switzerland.
More than half live in France, followed by Italy and Germany.
Geneva has the most cross-border commuters, while in Ticino they make up the largest share of all employees.
Cross-border commuters from abroad receive the G permit.
Cross-border commuters from the EU and EFTA must return to their place of residence at least once a week.
In Ticino they are called “frontalieri” in Italian.

abschnitte.text: A **cross-border commuter** lives in a neighbouring country and works in Switzerland. Many cross the border every day by car, train or bus. According to the **Federal Statistical Office (FSO)**, there were around **414,000** people in the second quarter of 2026. Their number has more than doubled since the mid-1990s.

More than half of the cross-border commuters live in **France**, above all around Geneva and Basel. **Italy** and **Germany** follow. The canton of **Geneva** is almost entirely surrounded by France and has the most cross-border commuters. In **Ticino** their share of all employees is the highest. Many of them commute from the provinces of Como, Varese and Verbano-Cusio-Ossola.

abschnitte.titel: The G permit and the rules
abschnitte.text: Anyone who works in Switzerland as a cross-border commuter gets the **G permit**, the cross-border commuter permit. Other permits are B for residence, C for settlement and L for short stays. For people from the **EU** and **EFTA**, it is enough to return to their place of residence abroad at least **once a week**. In the past, a daily return was required.

Where cross-border commuters pay tax is governed by **agreements** between the countries. With **Italy**, a new cross-border commuter agreement has applied since **July 2023**. Since then, new cross-border commuters have also been taxed more heavily in Italy. This changes how attractive a job in Ticino is for them.

Many cross-border commuters work in hospitals, in industry, in retail or on building sites. Since **December 2019**, the **Léman Express** suburban railway has linked Geneva with the surrounding French countryside. It is meant to move commuters from the car onto the railway. Cross-border commuters are also debated politically: some stress that the economy needs them, while others worry about traffic and wages.

gewusst: The word “frontalieri” comes from “frontiera”, the Italian word for border.
Three countries meet in the Basel region, so cross-border commuters from Germany and France come there.

teile.einleitung: The Alps did not simply grow upwards. During the formation of the mountains, huge slabs of rock were pushed over one another across long distances. Geologists call such slabs **nappes**.
wichtigste: A nappe is a large package of rock that has been pushed over other rocks.
The Alps arose when Europe and the Adriatic Plate collided.
From bottom to top in Switzerland come the Helvetic, the Penninic and the Austroalpine.
A klippe is an isolated remnant of a nappe, a window is a gap in a nappe.
In 1902 Maurice Lugeon summed up the nappe theory.
The summit of the Matterhorn belongs to the Austroalpine Dent Blanche Nappe.

abschnitte.text: A **nappe** is a slab of rock pushed far over other rocks. During the formation of the mountains large packages of rock broke away from their place of origin. They were pushed over many kilometres onto **foreign rocks**, like tablecloths pulled across a table. That is why in the Alps older rocks often lie above younger ones.

The Alps arose when the **Adriatic Plate**, also called the Apulian Plate, collided with the **European continental margin**. The Adriatic Plate is a spur of Africa. Between the two there used to be an ocean, which disappeared in the process. In front of the growing Alps, **flysch** was deposited in the sea, an alternating sequence of sandstone, marl and clay. Later it was itself overridden by nappes.

In the Swiss Alps three large nappe systems lie on top of one another. At the bottom lies the **Helvetic** with rocks from the European shelf, the shallow sea at the edge of Europe. Above it follows the **Penninic** from the former ocean area. At the top lies the **Austroalpine**, which comes from the Adriatic margin. South of the **Insubric Line** lie the **Southern Alps**, which were hardly pushed northwards at all.

Erosion has eaten into many nappes again. If only a separated remnant is left, lying on younger ground, it is called a **klippe**. If, conversely, a nappe has been worn away in one place so that you can see deeper units, this is called a **tectonic window**. A famous example is the **Tauern Window** in Austria.

The Lausanne geologist **Maurice Lugeon** put forward a comprehensive theory of the nappe structure of the Alps in **1902**. The Zurich geologist **Albert Heim** accepted it in the same year. A fine example is the **Matterhorn**. Its summit pyramid consists of gneisses of the **Dent Blanche Nappe**, which comes from the Adriatic continental margin.

gewusst: Because the summit rocks come from the Adriatic margin, people jokingly speak of the “African” summit of the Matterhorn.
Because of the nappes, older rocks in the Alps often lie above younger ones, that is, the opposite of what you would expect.

teile.einleitung: The **Dufourspitze** is the highest mountain in Switzerland. It lies in the canton of Valais and is the highest summit of the Monte Rosa massif. It bears its name in honour of General Guillaume-Henri Dufour.
wichtigste: At 4,634 metres the Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
It lies in the canton of Valais, not far from Zermatt.
It is the highest summit in the Monte Rosa massif on the border with Italy.
The summit itself lies entirely in Switzerland.
In the past the summit was simply called the “Highest Peak”.
In 1863 the Federal Council gave it the name Dufourspitze.

abschnitte.text: The **Dufourspitze** is **4,634 metres** high. No summit in Switzerland is higher. It lies in the **canton of Valais**, not far from the holiday resort of **Zermatt**. It is the highest summit in the great mountain massif of **Monte Rosa**. A massif is a group of connected mountains.

The **Monte Rosa massif** lies on the border between Switzerland and **Italy**. Many summits of the massif lie exactly on the border. The summit of the Dufourspitze, however, lies entirely in **Switzerland**, just beside the border. Around the mountain lie large glaciers, for example the Gorner Glacier.

In the past the summit was simply called the **“Highest Peak”**. In **1863** the **Federal Council** decided to name it after **General Guillaume-Henri Dufour** of Geneva. Dufour was an important officer and engineer. He led the work on the first accurate national map of Switzerland, the **Dufour Map**. With the name the Federal Council honoured the general and map-maker.

The Dufourspitze is a goal for experienced **mountaineers**. The route leads over glaciers and rocky ridges. For it you need good equipment, experience and usually a **mountain guide**. Most people spend the night beforehand in the **Monte Rosa Hut**. From the summit you can see far over the Valais and the Italian Alps.

gewusst: The highest mountain in Switzerland is named after a map-maker: General Dufour led the first accurate national map.
Before it received its name in 1863, the summit was quite simply called the “Highest Peak”.

teile.einleitung: **Emmental cheese** is a cheese from Switzerland that people all over the world recognise by its large holes. It comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern. A whole wheel is round like a wheel and very heavy.
wichtigste: You recognise Emmental cheese at once by its large, round holes.
It comes from the Emmental in the canton of Bern, the valley of the Emme.
Emmental cheese is made from raw cow’s milk.
A wheel weighs about 75 to 120 kilograms.
The holes arise from gas that bacteria form during ripening.
Young Emmental tastes mild and nutty.

abschnitte.text: Emmental cheese gets its name from the **Emmental**, a hilly area in the **canton of Bern**. The Emmental is the valley of the **Emme**. This river flows through the landscape and later joins the Aare. Today Emmental cheese is made in several regions of Switzerland, but the name recalls its home.

Emmental cheese is made from **raw cow’s milk**. Raw means that the milk is not strongly heated beforehand. The cows eat **grass and hay** for this, but no **silage**. Silage is fermented grass, which could spoil the cheese during ripening. The cheesemaker turns the milk into a wheel in a large vat.

Tiny **bacteria** live in the cheese. While the cheese ripens in the warm cellar, they form a **gas**. The gas cannot escape and collects in single places in the cheese. There the large, round **holes** arise. The firm outer layer, the **rind**, protects the cheese during ripening.

A whole wheel of Emmental cheese is round and flat like a big **wheel**. That is why people also speak of a **cheese wheel**. A wheel weighs about **75 to 120 kilograms**. This makes Emmental cheese one of the largest cheeses in the world. Young Emmental tastes **mild and slightly nutty**, older Emmental tastes stronger.

gewusst: A large wheel of Emmental cheese can be heavier than a grown-up person.
The holes in Emmental cheese are made by bacteria: they form a gas during ripening.

teile.einleitung: The Furka Pass is a high Alpine pass between the cantons of Uri and Valais. It is known for its winding road, the Rhône Glacier and a historic steam railway.
wichtigste: The Furka Pass links the cantons of Uri and Valais.
It lies at about 2,400 metres above sea level.
Right beside the pass lies the Rhône Glacier, where the Rhône rises.
At the eastern foot lies Realp in Uri, to the west the Goms in the Valais.
In summer a steam railway runs over the old mountain line.
In winter a car-carrying train takes vehicles through the tunnel under the Furka.

abschnitte.text: The **Furka Pass** lies at about **2,429 m above sea level** and links the cantons of **Uri** and **Valais**. At the eastern foot lies the Uri village of **Realp**, to the west the Valais valley region of **Goms**. The pass road has many tight bends. In winter it is closed because of snow.

Right beside the pass lies the **Rhône Glacier**. From its meltwater the **Rhône** rises, which flows through the Valais into Lake Geneva and on to France. By the road stands the **Hotel Belvédère** with a view of the glacier. Because the glacier has shrunk a lot, you can see the ice from the hotel much less well today than in the past.

In the past the railway ran over the top of the pass. Since 1982 the trains have gone through the **Furka Base Tunnel**. On the old **mountain line** a historic **steam railway** runs in summer, operated by many volunteers. In winter a **car train** takes cars through the tunnel between Realp and Oberwald.

The Furka Pass is also a film star. In the **James Bond film** “Goldfinger” of 1964 the agent drives a sports car over the pass road. Since then many fans have come to drive the route themselves. Cyclists and motorcyclists love the bends too.

gewusst: The Furka mountain line steam railway uses locomotives, some of which were brought back to Switzerland from Vietnam.
The name Furka means fork, because the pass lies like a fork between two peaks.

teile.einleitung: The region around Zug, where many companies for **blockchain** and **cryptocurrencies** have settled, is called the **Crypto Valley**. The name recalls Silicon Valley in California. Here you can find out how it came about.
wichtigste: The centre of the Crypto Valley is the canton of Zug.
Since about 2014 many blockchain companies have settled there.
The Ethereum Foundation was founded in Zug in 2014.
From 2016 you could pay small fees in the city of Zug with Bitcoin.
Since 2017 the Crypto Valley Association has represented the companies of the region.
In 2021 the DLT Act came into force.

abschnitte.text: A **blockchain** is a kind of digital account book. The entries are not stored in one single place but on many computers at the same time. This is called **distributed ledger technology**, or **DLT** for short. The blockchain is its best-known form. **Cryptocurrencies** such as Bitcoin are based on it.

Since about **2014** many blockchain and crypto companies have settled in the **canton of Zug**. The starting point is considered to be the founding of the **Ethereum Foundation** in Zug in 2014. This foundation supports the development of the Ethereum blockchain. Zug attracted companies with **low taxes**, an **open administration** and its **closeness to the financial centre of Zurich**.

The city of Zug showed early that it is open to new technologies. From **July 2016** you could pay smaller administrative fees with **Bitcoin**. That was one of the first examples in the world of an authority accepting a cryptocurrency. In 2017 the **Crypto Valley Association** was founded. This association links companies, research and authorities.

In an **initial coin offering**, or **ICO** for short, a project sells digital **tokens**, mostly for cryptocurrencies, in order to raise money. Many Zug blockchain projects financed themselves this way around 2017. Because it was new, it was unclear which rules applied. In February 2018 **FINMA**, the Swiss financial market supervisory authority, published a **guide** on it. This created more legal certainty.

The Confederation also adapted the law. In **2021** the so-called **DLT Act** came into force. Its full name is the Federal Act on the Adaptation of Federal Law to Developments in Distributed Ledger Technology. Among other things it created **digital register rights**, that is, securities that are entered on a blockchain. Cryptocurrencies remain risky, however, because their value can fluctuate strongly.

gewusst: Zug was one of the first authorities in the world to accept Bitcoin as a means of payment for fees.
The name Crypto Valley is an allusion to the famous Silicon Valley in the USA.

teile.einleitung: A border river is a river along which a border runs. Switzerland has many such rivers, above all the Rhine in the north, which forms the border with Germany over long stretches.
wichtigste: With a border river, the two banks lie in different countries or cantons.
The border usually runs down the middle of the river.
Between Lake Constance and Basel, the High Rhine largely forms the border with Germany.
There are many river power stations on the High Rhine, often run jointly by both countries.
In the west of the canton of Geneva, the Rhône forms a stretch of the border with France.
Ponte Tresa lies on the Tresa on the border with Italy.

abschnitte.text: A **border river** separates two countries, cantons or municipalities from each other. One **bank** belongs to one area, the other bank to the other. The border usually runs down the **middle of the river**. Rivers work well as borders because they are easy to recognise. In the past they were also hard to cross.

The **High Rhine** flows from the Untersee near **Stein am Rhein** to **Basel**. Over long stretches it forms the border between Switzerland and **Germany**. In several places **river power stations** stand right across the river, for example near **Rheinfelden**. Because the border runs through the water, such power stations often belong to both countries together.

On some border rivers, two places lie directly opposite each other. There are two **Laufenburgs**: Laufenburg in Aargau and Laufenburg in Baden on the German side. A bridge links the two. On the **Tresa** in Ticino, too, the Swiss **Ponte Tresa** and the Italian **Lavena Ponte Tresa** face each other. A border crossing leads over the bridge.

abschnitte.titel: The Rhône and other border rivers
abschnitte.text: Shortly before the **Rhône** leaves Switzerland, it forms the border with **France** in the west of the canton of Geneva. The joint power station **Chancy-Pougny** stands there. In the Jura, the **Doubs** forms a stretch of the border with France. In the east, the **Alpine Rhine** separates Switzerland from Liechtenstein and Austria.

abschnitte.titel: The Rhine Falls are not a border
abschnitte.text: Although the Rhine often forms the border in the Schaffhausen region, the **Rhine Falls** are not a border waterfall. On one bank lies **Neuhausen** in the canton of Schaffhausen, on the other **Laufen-Uhwiesen** in the canton of Zurich. So both banks belong to Switzerland. There, however, the Rhine is a **cantonal border**.

gewusst: The canton of Schaffhausen lies mostly north of the Rhine and is almost completely surrounded by Germany.
Cantons have border rivers too: at the Rhine Falls the Rhine separates Schaffhausen and Zurich.

teile.einleitung: The Folded Jura is the part of the Jura Mountains in which the layers of rock were pushed together like a tablecloth. In this way long, parallel mountain ridges and valleys arose in the north-west of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Folded Jura arose when layers of rock were pushed together.
The thrust came from the formation of the Alps and was transmitted underneath the Central Plateau.
The layers slid on soft layers of salt and anhydrite from the Triassic.
Upward-arching folds are called anticlines, the troughs between them synclines.
A Klus is a transverse valley through which a river breaks through a ridge.
At 1,607 m the Chasseral is the highest summit of the Bernese Jura.

abschnitte.text: If you push a tablecloth together on a table, waves appear. Something similar happened to the **limestone layers** of the Jura. The pressure of the **formation of the Alps** was passed on underneath the Central Plateau as far as the Jura. This is called **long-distance thrust**. In this way the layers folded into long ridges.

Under the limestone layers lie soft **layers of salt and anhydrite** from the **Triassic**, a geological period over 200 million years ago. They worked like a lubricant. On them the whole stack of rock could slide off and fold into waves. The base underneath was hardly folded along with it.

A fold arching upwards is called an **anticline**, or vault. It forms a mountain ridge. The troughs between them are called **synclines** and form the longitudinal valleys. If erosion has broken open the crest of a vault and cleared out the soft core, a **combe** arises.

Some rivers break right across a Jura ridge. Such a narrow transverse valley is called a **Klus** (plural **Klusen**). Well-known examples are near **Balsthal** and **Moutier**. Klusen are important transport routes, because roads and railways can cross the ridges there.

The **Chasseral** at 1,607 m above sea level is the highest summit of the Bernese Jura. It lies between Lake Biel and the Vallon de Saint-Imier. The **Val de Travers** in the Neuchâtel Jura is regarded as the home of **absinthe**, a herbal spirit that was first made there at the end of the 18th century.

gewusst: The word Klus comes from the Latin clausa, which means roughly “closed place”.
The name Jura stands worldwide for a whole geological period, the Jurassic, named after this mountain range.

teile.einleitung: The **Creux du Van** is a huge rock amphitheatre in the Neuchâtel Jura. Its steep limestone cliffs form a semicircle and are among the best-known natural wonders of Switzerland. At the top, on the rim, there is a wide view.
wichtigste: The Creux du Van lies above the Val de Travers in the canton of Neuchâtel.
The rock walls fall about 160 metres vertically.
The rock circle is around 4 kilometres long in total.
The amphitheatre probably formed after the last cold period through erosion.
The spring Fontaine Froide has water of about 4 °C all year round.
Ibex and chamois live in the rocks.
The area has been protected since 1972.

abschnitte.text: The **limestone cliffs** of the Creux du Van fall about **160 metres** vertically. Together they form a semicircle around **4 kilometres** long. The amphitheatre is about 1,200 metres wide and 500 metres deep. It lies above the **Val de Travers**, near the border with the canton of Vaud. From **Noiraigue** a steep walking path leads up.

According to present views, the rock amphitheatre probably formed after the **Würm glaciation**, the last great cold period. **Erosion** means that rock is slowly worn away. At the Creux du Van it was above all **frost** and **water** that broke the rock up and carried it away. In this way the great circle came about over time.

Down in the shady amphitheatre lies the spring **Fontaine Froide**. The name means “cold fountain”. Its water is an even **4 °C** cold all year round. In the amphitheatre it is often much cooler than in the surroundings. That is why plants also grow there that otherwise occur more at higher altitudes.

In the rock walls you often see **ibex** and **chamois**. They are skilful climbers and find shelter on the rock ledges. Often they can be watched from close up. In **1974 and 1975** a pair of **lynx** from the Slovak Carpathians was released in each of two years in the region. In this way the lynx was meant to return to the Jura.

Since **1972** the area of the Creux du Van has been under **protection**. It also belongs to the **Federal Inventory of Landscapes** of national importance. Visitors should stay on the paths and not disturb the animals. At the edge of the cliffs care is important, because there is not a railing everywhere.

gewusst: The rock walls of the Creux du Van are about as high as a tower block with around 50 floors.
The spring Fontaine Froide stays only about 4 °C cold even in the hottest summer.

teile.einleitung: Every country has points that lie furthest north, south, west and east. In addition there are the highest and the lowest point. They are called the extreme points of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The northernmost point lies near Bargen in the canton of Schaffhausen.
The southernmost point lies near Pedrinate, a part of Chiasso in Ticino.
The westernmost point lies near Chancy in the canton of Geneva.
The easternmost point lies on the Piz Chavalatsch in the Val Müstair in Graubünden.
The highest point is the Dufourspitze at 4,634 m, the lowest is Lake Maggiore at 193 m.
The difference in height is about 4,440 metres.

abschnitte.text: The northernmost point of Switzerland lies near **Oberbargen** in the municipality of **Bargen** in the canton of **Schaffhausen**. Schaffhausen lies north of the Rhine and is almost completely surrounded by Germany. There you are already further north than in many parts of southern Germany.
The southernmost point lies near **Pedrinate**, a part of **Chiasso** in the canton of **Ticino**. Italy begins right behind it. In the south of Ticino the climate is mild, and even palm trees grow.

Right in the west lies the Geneva municipality of **Chancy** on the Rhône, surrounded by France. Right in the east lies the **Piz Chavalatsch** in the municipality of **Val Müstair** in the canton of Graubünden, on the border with Italy. Between these two points there are about 350 kilometres as the crow flies.

abschnitte.titel: Right at the top and right at the bottom
abschnitte.text: The highest point is the **Dufourspitze** in the Monte Rosa massif in the Valais at **4,634 m above sea level**. The lowest point is the surface of **Lake Maggiore** in Ticino at about **193 m above sea level**. If you subtract the two numbers from each other, you get a difference of about **4,441 metres**. So in a small space there are huge differences in height.

gewusst: From Lake Maggiore with its palm trees to the glaciers of the Dufourspitze it is only a good 100 kilometres as the crow flies.
All four extreme points in the compass directions lie directly on the national border.

teile.einleitung: The Grande Dixence is a huge dam in the canton of Valais. It is the tallest gravity dam in the world and holds back the Lac des Dix, the largest reservoir in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Grande Dixence stands in the Val d'Hérémence in the canton of Valais.
The dam is 285 metres high.
It is the tallest gravity dam in the world.
Behind the wall lies the Lac des Dix, about 5 kilometres long.
The lake holds around 400 million cubic metres of water.
Most of the water is meltwater from glaciers.

abschnitte.text: The **Grande Dixence** is **285 metres** high. That is almost as tall as the Eiffel Tower in Paris. More than **6 million cubic metres of concrete** went into the wall. It weighs about **15 million tonnes**. It was built in the 1950s, and over 3,000 workers were involved. It stands high up in the **Val d'Hérémence**, a side valley in the Valais.

There are different kinds of dam. An **arch dam** is curved and pushes the force of the water sideways into the rocks. A **gravity dam**, by contrast, holds back the water with its own enormous **weight**. That is why it is very thick at the bottom. No other gravity dam in the world is as tall as the Grande Dixence.

Behind the wall lies the **Lac des Dix**. “Dix” is the name of the valley and here does not mean the number ten. The lake is about **5 kilometres** long. When it is full, its water level is at around **2,364 metres** above sea level. It holds around **400 million cubic metres** of water, more than any other reservoir in Switzerland.

Most of the water comes from **glaciers**. In summer a lot of ice melts in the mountains around the valley. The **meltwater** is collected and led into the lake through long tunnels. In summer the lake fills, and in winter the water is used. That is when Switzerland needs particularly large amounts of electricity.

The water from the Lac des Dix flows through pipes and tunnels down to **power stations** in the Rhône Valley. There it drives **turbines** that generate electricity. Because the water falls a very long way, it produces a lot of power. **Hydropower** is the most important source of electricity in Switzerland. Visitors can look round the wall in summer.

gewusst: At 285 metres, the Grande Dixence is the tallest structure in Switzerland.
In summer you can walk through passages inside the dam.

teile.einleitung: The geographical centre of Switzerland lies on the Älggi Alp above Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden. It was calculated in 1988 by the Federal Office of Topography.
wichtigste: The centre was calculated in 1988.
The occasion was the 150th anniversary of the Federal Office of Topography.
It was determined as the centre of gravity of the country's area.
It lies in the Alps, in the municipality of Sachseln in the canton of Obwalden.
The memorial stone stands at around 1,650 m above sea level on the Älggi Alp.
The exact point is hard to reach, so the stone stands a little way off.

abschnitte.text: The **Federal Office of Topography**, today called swisstopo, was founded in **1838**. For its **150th birthday** in **1988** it calculated the centre of Switzerland. It used the national borders of the time. Since then the place has been a popular destination for outings.

They determined the **centre of gravity of the country's area**. Imagine you cut Switzerland out of cardboard. At this point you could **balance the cardboard Switzerland on the tip of a needle**. There are other ways of finding a centre, so this point is a matter of definition.

The calculated point lies above a **rock face** and is hard to reach. That is why the **memorial stone** stands about 500 metres away on an alpine pasture. It lies at around **1,650 m above sea level** on the **Älggi Alp** above **Sachseln**. So the centre lies right in the middle of the **Alps**.

The municipality of Sachseln has more than just the centre. **Niklaus von Flüe**, known as **Brother Klaus**, is buried in the parish church. He lived as a hermit in the Ranft in the 15th century and is the **national saint** of Switzerland. Many people make a pilgrimage to his grave.

gewusst: If you counted the lakes differently or chose another method, you would arrive at a slightly different place.
The centre is not in a town or city, but on a remote alpine pasture.

teile.einleitung: Delémont, in German **Delsberg**, is the main town of the canton of Jura. The town lies in the Jura on the Sorne and is the largest municipality of the youngest Swiss canton.
wichtigste: The official name is Delémont, Delsberg is the German name.
Delémont is the main town and largest municipality of the canton of Jura.
The town lies on the Sorne shortly before it flows into the Birs.
At the end of 2023 around 12,700 people lived in Delémont.
Every year in September the Fête du peuple jurassien takes place.

abschnitte.titel: Position on the Sorne and the Birs
abschnitte.text: Delémont lies in a wide valley in the **Jura**. The town lies on both sides of the **Sorne**, shortly before it flows into the **Birs**. The Birs flows on towards Basel and enters the Rhine there. In the canton of Jura people speak **French**, so the town is officially called **Delémont**.

abschnitte.titel: Main town of the canton of Jura
abschnitte.text: Delémont is the **main town** of the canton of Jura. The government and parliament of the canton have their seat here. At the end of **2023**, **12,739** people lived in Delémont. That is few compared with other cantonal capitals, yet Delémont is the **largest municipality** of the canton. The old town with its castle and fountains is well preserved.

Every year in **September** the **Fête du peuple jurassien** takes place in Delémont, the festival of the Jura people. It has been held since **1947**. The festival recalls the long political struggle for a **canton of Jura** of its own. The canton came into being after popular votes and since 1979 has been the youngest canton of Switzerland.

gewusst: The canton of Jura with its main town Delémont has been the youngest canton of Switzerland since 1979.
The Fête du peuple jurassien has been celebrated since 1947, long before the canton existed.
